### Global Metadata
A complete 100-second warm evening summer-festival piece (natsu matsuri feeling) for a small neighborhood market at sunset in a Japanese town: paper lanterns lighting up, neighbors chatting, cicadas in the distance. 100 BPM, C major pentatonic (yo scale), festive but relaxed and cozy, never loud or aggressive. Shinobue bamboo flute melody, koto and shamisen plucked patterns, gentle taiko and small hand drums, light chappa hand cymbals, soft hand claps, round acoustic bass and a warm string pad. Natural outdoor-evening acoustic, warm golden tone, clear mix. Pure instrumental folk-ensemble piece. Avoid EDM drops, trap hi-hats, distorted guitars, heavy sub bass, trailer braams and cinematic bombast. No rock drum kit.

### Vocal Details
None. Instrumental only: the shinobue leads with graceful ornaments; the koto answers in call-and-response.

### Timed Arrangement
0-12 seconds: koto and shamisen set a lilting festival rhythm with soft taiko. 12-44 seconds: the shinobue plays a memorable pentatonic theme, hand claps on beats two and four. 44-76 seconds: koto takes the theme, flute adds decorative runs, a warm string pad supports the harmony. 76-98 seconds: a slightly fuller section with taiko fills and chappa, still gentle. 98-110 seconds: return to the flute theme and finish on the tonic without a fade so it can loop. Keep tempo and loudness steady throughout. The piece must play for the full 100 seconds and must not end early.
